guidelines.detail: same as LRN-062 (Two reference activities that perform a check before an exclusive decision (M1: the stock check for the first item; M2: the readiness check for the set of items after the registration step) are absent from the generated model, while the description states both checks explicitly (S2, S7) and the decision on each follows from the check (S2 and S9 loop back to the check for the next item). LRN-062 al)

same as LRN-062 (Two reference activities that check a product's stock status and whether the whole order is ready are missing from the generated model. The description states both checks as steps before a decision (S2, S7), and the next product loop (S9) depends on the check result. LRN-062 already requires a separate check activity before the branching gateway, but it is narrowly framed around a participant chec)

same as LRN-096 (The reference has an exclusive gateway ('Arrived after more than ten days?') after the wait, which the generated model lacks (M1). Instead it attaches a timer boundary event 'Waiting more than 10 days' to the wait (X2) and ends the process in a separate 'Penalty demanded' end event (X3). The description (S5) says the wait continues until arrival, the action is taken only if the wait exceeds the du)

same as LRN-094 (The reference starts the process with a single start event that flows directly into the first read activity (M1, F4). The generated model instead creates a start event named 'Order received' that sits before that read (X1, G1), which is an extra entry point for a derived state of the input. The description states no separate trigger for the process, only that the first activity is reading the orde)

same as LRN-094 (The reference has a start event labeled with the title before the first task, and the generated model has no counterpart (M1). The description gives a title and opens with an action, with no separate trigger (S1). LRN-094 already requires one start event at the process entry before the first action task, and LRN-008 covers the same pattern, so this guideline restates them with the title-label conv)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says a participant first checks whether they already have something, and a later exclusive decision branches on the result of that check: Model the check as its own activity performed by that participant, labeled with the description's own wording for the check, placed after the preceding step and before the exclusive gateway that branches on the result. Do not drop the check or fold it into the gateway's label or condition, and do not model it as a gateway.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that an item, or a set of items, is checked against a condition, and an exclusive decision then branches on the outcome of that check, possibly with repetition over further items

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that a wait for an awaited item continues until the item is received, and that an extra action is taken only if that wait lasted longer than a stated duration: Model the wait as a single receiving activity with no timer boundary event attached to it. Place an exclusive gateway directly after the receiving activity, phrased as a question about whether the stated duration was exceeded. Route the exceeded branch into the extra action, and route the extra action onward to the step where the normal path continues. Route the not-exceeded branch directly to that same continuation point, so that both branches rejoin before the next described step.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that a wait for an awaited item continues until the item is received, and that an extra action is taken only if that wait lasted longer than a stated duration

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that the flow begins with an actor's own action, with no separate triggering event or message described before it, and a later check of that action follows: Model exactly one start event at the process entry. Connect it by a sequence flow to a bpmn:task for the actor's stated action, and never model that action as a start event. Do not add further start events for later checks or later phases, and do not connect the start event directly to a check the description places after the action. A later phase begins from the outgoing flow of the preceding step to a task for its first activity.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description has a title and its first sentence states an activity that retrieves input from another system (for example, reading data from an external management system), and it describes no separate event that starts the process
